text: This sends an A-valued Hopf-algebra point to its tensor-compatible action on every finitely generated comodule, matching [Milne 9.2(a–c)](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175). Points multiply by convolution; their images compose with the right factor acting first. The source proves the homomorphism laws by forgetting the tensor proofs, without claiming injectivity or reconstruction here. Checks pass: [fgPointTensorIsoHom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L637), [scalarExtensionComponent_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L311).
Checks the actual function underlying the homomorphism.
Checks composition order on transported components.

A point acts naturally on each scalar-extended comodule, preserves the tensor unit, and respects tensor products. These are precisely [Milne 9.2(a–c)](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175), used here to package a tensor automorphism. The source verifies both comparisons over commutative semirings; H itself need not be commutative, and no reconstruction assertion is included. Checks pass: [fgPointTensorIso_hom_hom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L591), [fgPointTensorIso_inv_hom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L612).
Checks the forward natural transformation is unchanged by packaging.
Checks the inverse natural transformation is unchanged too.

Evaluating the point-to-tensor-automorphism homomorphism gives exactly the previously constructed tensor automorphism. This is a definitional equation: adding the homomorphism laws leaves the point action unchanged. Its mathematical content is the canonical assignment in [Milne 9.2](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175), with the source retaining explicit scalar extension and convolution multiplication. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionComponent_fgPointTensorIso](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L598), [fgPointTensorIso_hom_hom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L591).
Checks its actual action on each scalar-extended module.
Checks the underlying natural transformation.

Forgetting the tensor-compatibility proof recovers the original natural automorphism induced by the point. A monoidal natural transformation consists of its ordinary natural transformation plus compatibility conditions, as in [EGNO 1.5.1](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=15). The nested hom projections forget structure; they do not change the point action or its direction. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionComponent_fgPointTensorIso](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L598), [fgPointTensorIso_inv_hom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L612).
Checks the resulting linear components.
Checks the corresponding statement for the inverse.

Two tensor automorphisms are equal if their A-linear maps on every A⊗M are equal. Equality identifications are invertible, so cancelling them recovers equality of all natural-transformation components. The tensor conditions are properties, not extra maps. This agrees with [EGNO’s morphism definition](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=15); equality at only one chosen comodule is not assumed sufficient. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionComponent_one](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L296), [scalarExtensionComponent_monoidalAutOfComponents](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L510).
Checks transport of the identity.
Checks recovery of an explicitly assembled family.

The natural point action is monoidal because it is identity on the trivial comodule and intertwines the tensor comparison. These are the two compatibility conditions in [EGNO 1.5.1–2](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=15), also [Milne 9.2(a–b)](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175). Naturality is already supplied by the given natural automorphism; the proof adds the unit and tensor laws. Checks pass: [ofLinearEquiv_pointsAction_tensorUnit_eq_one](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L541), [distribBaseChange_comp_pointsAction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L555).
Checks the unit condition.
Checks the tensor condition.

This extracts the A-linear component of a tensor automorphism on A⊗M, using equality identifications to expose the functor’s chosen object. It is the explicit component of [EGNO’s monoidal natural transformation](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=15). Although returned as a linear map, it is invertible because the original component is; no basis or additional choice of isomorphism is made. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionComponent_one](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L296), [scalarExtensionComponent_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L311).
Checks identity transport.
Checks compatibility with composition.

Under the canonical identification (A⊗M)⊗_A(A⊗N)≅A⊗(M⊗N), acting by g on both factors equals acting on their tensor product. This is [Milne’s tensor condition 9.2(a)](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175). Its source proof uses multiplicativity of the algebra-valued point; the order of the H-coefficients is preserved, so H need not be commutative. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_tensor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L359), [scalarExtensionComponent_fgPointTensorIso](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L598).
Checks the underlying linear-map tensor identity.
Checks that the packaged point components are these maps.

An existing natural automorphism becomes monoidal when its identified linear components fix the tensor unit and satisfy the displayed tensor-comparison square. These are exactly [EGNO 1.5.1–2](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=15). The hypotheses identify the family with the automorphism and explicitly supply both laws; arbitrary unrelated linear automorphisms would not suffice. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionComponent_monoidalAutOfComponents](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L510), [scalarExtensionComponent_tensorUnit](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L366).
Checks assembly from such a family recovers its components.
Checks the resulting unit consequence.

On the tensor unit—the base semiring with trivial coaction—every algebra-valued point acts as identity after scalar extension. Applying g to the coaction coefficient 1 gives 1. This is [Milne 9.2(b)](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175); the symbol 1 in the general linear group means the identity operator, not a scalar-valued map. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_trivial](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L574), [scalarExtensionComponent_tensorUnit](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L366).
Checks the underlying action on the trivial comodule.
Checks the same unit condition for general tensor automorphisms.

The explicit component of the tensor automorphism attached to g is exactly its usual point action on A⊗M. The proof cancels the equality identifications around the natural component. This supplies the concrete meaning of the assignment in [Milne 9.2](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175), without asserting that all tensor automorphisms arise from points over these general semirings. Checks pass: [fgPointTensorIso_hom_hom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L591), [localFunctional_fgPointTensorIso](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/LocalFunctional.lean#L217).
Checks forgetting tensor compatibility.
Checks counit evaluation recovers the point on finite regular subcomodules in the stated field specialization.

For a comodule morphism f:M→N, the components commute with its scalar extension: f_A η_M=η_N f_A. This is [Milne 9.2(c)](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175). The source removes the functor-object identifications from naturality; f must preserve the coaction, so the claim does not require commutation with every underlying linear map. Checks pass: [localFunctional_eq_comp_inclusion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/LocalFunctional.lean#L182), [scalarExtensionComponent_fgPointTensorIso](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L598).
Checks its use for finite regular-subcomodule inclusions.
Checks the concrete point-action components.

The component on M⊗N sends the tensor of x and y to the tensor of their respective images, after the canonical scalar-extension comparison. This is the commuting square of [EGNO 1.5.1](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=15). Here x and y are arbitrary elements of A⊗M and A⊗N; neither is required to be a pure tensor over R. Checks pass: [distribBaseChange_comp_scalarExtensionComponent](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L393), [distribBaseChange_comp_pointsAction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L555).
Checks the equivalent identity of linear maps.
Checks the point-action instance.

This evaluates the extracted component by identifying A⊗M with the functor object, applying the natural automorphism, and identifying back. The equality follows directly from the definition and makes the component of [EGNO’s natural transformation](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=15) explicit. These equality transports change packaging only; no arbitrary coordinate system is introduced. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionComponent_one](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L296), [scalarExtensionComponent_fgPointTensorIso](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L598).
Checks cancellation of the identifications for identity.
Checks cancellation for a point action.

If the natural-transformation component is the displayed transport of an invertible linear map F, extracting its component gives F itself. The explicit hypothesis supplies that identification; the proof cancels the forward and backward transports. This matches the underlying-component interpretation in [EGNO 1.5.1](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=15), without asserting equality for an unrelated F. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionComponent_monoidalAutOfComponents](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L510), [scalarExtensionComponent_fgPointTensorIso](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L598).
Checks the family-construction application.
Checks the point-action application.

For a finite regular subcomodule N, this sends n to counit evaluation of η_N(1⊗n). It is k-linear by composition, realizing the local evaluation-at-identity step behind [Milne 9.1–2](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175). Finite means finitely generated as a module; N need not be a subalgebra, and multiplicativity is not asserted for this local functional. Checks pass: [localFunctional_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/LocalFunctional.lean#L170), [localFunctional_eq_comp_inclusion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/LocalFunctional.lean#L182).
Checks the defining evaluation formula.
Checks compatibility as the chosen finite subcomodule grows.

When N⊆Q, the functional extracted on N is the restriction of the one on Q. Naturality makes η commute with the inclusion, and the restricted counits agree. This matches the compatibility step in [Milne’s proof of 9.2](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=176); the theorem supplies local agreement, without assuming these subcomodules already cover H. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionComponent_natural](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L140), [localFunctional_fgPointTensorIso](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/LocalFunctional.lean#L217).
Checks the naturality square used for inclusion.
Checks compatibility with actual point restrictions in the field specialization.

Over the stated field, extracting the local functional from a point-induced tensor automorphism returns g(n). Applying the counit to the regular coaction recovers n, so the evaluation formula yields exactly g(n). This is the evaluation-at-identity mechanism of [Milne 9.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175); the declaration assumes a commutative Hopf algebra and commutative value algebra. Checks pass: [matrixCoefficient_counit_comp_subtype](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Regular.lean#L58), [baseChangeEvaluation_endOfPoint_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Evaluation.lean#L65).
Checks that the restricted-counit matrix coefficient is n.
Checks evaluation of a point action against a functional.

This is the A-linear extension of the counit restricted to N: a⊗n maps to a·ε(n), with ε(n) mapped into A. It is the linear evaluation-at-identity operation underlying [Milne 9.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175). Only a coalgebra is needed here; no multiplication on H, finiteness of N, or flatness is assumed. Checks pass: [counitEvaluation_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/LocalFunctional.lean#L78), [counitEvaluation_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/LocalFunctional.lean#L85).
Checks the value on pure tensors.
Checks identification with the base-changed restricted counit.

On a pure tensor, counit evaluation is a·algebraMap(ε(n)). This follows by extending the restricted counit linearly and is the scalar-extension form of evaluation at identity in [Milne 9.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175). The algebra map is essential because ε(n) lies in the base semiring, while the result lies in A. Checks pass: [baseChangeEvaluation_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Dual/BaseChange.lean#L68), [counitEvaluation_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/LocalFunctional.lean#L85).
Checks the general pairing formula specialized to the restricted counit.
Checks the full linear-map characterization.

A finitely generated subcomodule of the regular comodule is bundled as an object of the finite-comodule category. This is the local regular-representation object used in [Milne’s proof of 9.2](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=176). Finite refers to module generators, not cardinality; the assumed semiring flatness preserves injections so the restricted coaction is available. Checks pass: [regularInclusion_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/LocalFunctional.lean#L137), [localFunctional_fgPointTensorIso](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/LocalFunctional.lean#L217).
Checks inclusions between these bundled objects.
Checks point recovery on such an object in the field specialization.

The extracted functional evaluates n by first forming 1⊗n, then applying the automorphism component on N, then applying the restricted counit. The formula directly exposes the definition and its order, matching the evaluation-at-identity step in [Milne 9.1–2](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175). Restricting scalars records k-linearity without changing these functions. Checks pass: [localFunctional_eq_comp_inclusion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/LocalFunctional.lean#L182), [localFunctional_fgPointTensorIso](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/LocalFunctional.lean#L217).
Checks that this formula respects inclusions.
Checks its value for an actual point in the field specialization.

For N⊆Q, the ordinary subtype inclusion is promoted to a comodule morphism between the finite regular objects. The induced coactions agree after embedding into H⊗H; Module.Flat here means tensoring with H preserves injections, permitting cancellation. This supplies the equivariant inclusion used in [Milne’s local compatibility argument](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=176), with finite meaning finitely generated. Checks pass: [regularInclusion_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/LocalFunctional.lean#L137), [regularInclusion_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/LocalFunctional.lean#L147).
Checks the underlying function.
Checks the underlying linear map.

Forgetting coaction compatibility from the finite regular-subcomodule inclusion gives exactly the ordinary submodule inclusion N→Q. The equality is definitional: the categorical constructor stores that linear map. It identifies the concrete inclusion used for the naturality step of [Milne’s reconstruction proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=176), while retaining the stated flatness assumption for the comodule structures. Checks pass: [regularInclusion_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/LocalFunctional.lean#L137), [localFunctional_eq_comp_inclusion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/LocalFunctional.lean#L182).
Checks the pointwise inclusion.
Checks its use in restriction of the local functionals.

Counit evaluation equals base change of ε restricted to N, followed by the tensor-unit identification A⊗k≅A. Thus it is independent of any expression of z as a sum of pure tensors. This is the scalar-extended linear version of evaluation at identity in [Milne 9.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175); it does not require N to be finite or flat. Checks pass: [counitEvaluation_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/LocalFunctional.lean#L78), [baseChangeEvaluation_one_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Dual/BaseChange.lean#L62).
Checks the characteristic formula on generators.
Checks that evaluation by 1⊗φ is the base-changed functional.

Converting a nonnegative real r to the nonnegative-real type and then back to the reals recovers r. The hypothesis includes zero and prevents information loss: the conversion is max(r,0), so a negative input would return zero instead. The result identifies the ordinary inclusion on its intended nonnegative domain, without asserting a global inverse. Compared with [Faris §8.1 p88](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L161).

Replacing a real number by its nonnegative part never decreases it: r≤max(r,0). This holds without a sign assumption. Nonnegative inputs stay unchanged, while negative inputs increase to zero. The final value is viewed as an ordinary real, so the comparison involves no infinity and does not assert equality for negative inputs. Compared with [Faris §8.1 p88](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L167).

For a nonnegative-real value r and a real p≥0, the inequality r≤p.toNNReal is equivalent to the ordinary real inequality r≤p. The sign assumption is on p, the converted upper bound. Without it, r=0 and p=−1 would make the converted inequality true and the original real inequality false. Compared with [Faris §8.1 p88](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L679).

The nonnegative part of a real number is strictly positive exactly when the original number is strictly positive. Negative values and zero all become zero, so they fail both sides of this positivity test. This is stronger than merely saying the output is nonnegative, which is automatic from the target type. Compared with [Faris §8.1 p88](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L551).

Taking nonnegative parts preserves addition when both summands are already nonnegative. Under those hypotheses neither the summands nor their sum is changed by clipping at zero. The assumptions matter: for −1 and 2, the nonnegative part of their sum is 1, while the sum of their nonnegative parts is 2. Compared with [Faris §8.1 p88](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L662).

Taking nonnegative parts commutes with multiplication when the first factor is nonnegative; the second factor may have either sign. A negative second factor makes both sides zero, while nonnegative factors are unchanged. The restriction cannot be dropped: multiplying −1 by −1 gives positive part 1, whereas their separate positive parts multiply to zero. Compared with [Faris §8.1 p88](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L699).

A real number’s nonnegative part is at most a nonnegative-real bound p exactly when the original real number is at most p. No sign assumption on the real input is needed: if it is negative, it and its clipped value zero are both below p. The bound’s nonnegativity is supplied by its type. Compared with [Faris §8.1 p88](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L676).

Clipping real numbers at zero preserves non-strict order: if r≤p, then max(r,0)≤max(p,0). Neither input needs to be nonnegative. This is monotonicity, not strict monotonicity or injectivity: different negative inputs have the same output zero, so strict inequalities and distinctions between them may disappear after conversion. Compared with [Faris §8.1 p88](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L670).

Subtracting nonnegative reals and then viewing the result as a real agrees with ordinary real subtraction when the subtrahend does not exceed the minuend. That hypothesis prevents truncation. Without it, subtraction in the nonnegative-real type stops at zero: 1−2 there becomes 0, whereas ordinary real subtraction gives −1. Compared with [Faris §2.5](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L229).

Viewing a nonnegative real’s reciprocal as an ordinary real gives the same reciprocal. This includes zero because Lean defines 0⁻¹=0 in both the real and nonnegative-real types. The identity therefore needs no nonzero hypothesis; it does not assert that zero has a multiplicative inverse, or use the extended-nonnegative convention 0⁻¹=∞. Compared with [Faris §2.5](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L219).

Dividing two nonnegative reals and then including the result in the reals agrees with ordinary real division. No denominator restriction is imposed because both Lean types define division by zero to be zero. For positive denominators this is the usual quotient; the zero case is a shared default, not an assertion of ordinary division being defined there. Compared with [Faris §2.5](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L223).

The infimum of any family of nonnegative reals has the same value when computed in the nonnegative reals or in the reals. Every nonempty family is bounded below by zero. Empty families are also allowed: Lean assigns their infimum zero in both types, so this case records matching defaults rather than a genuine greatest lower bound. Compared with [Faris §§2.7,5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L490).

For two nonnegative real inputs, conversion into extended nonnegative reals preserves and reflects equality. Both outputs are finite and retain their original values. The sign assumptions prevent the collapse of negative inputs to zero: without them, distinct inputs such as −1 and −2 would have equal converted values despite being unequal as real numbers. Compared with [Faris §8.1 p88](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L162).

If the upper input q is nonnegative, comparing the converted values is equivalent to p≤q in the reals. The lower input p may be negative: its converted value is then zero, still at most the converted q. Requiring q≥0 prevents the false reverse comparison that occurs when both inputs are clipped to zero. Compared with [Faris §8.1 p88](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L147).

Without sign assumptions, converted values satisfy ofReal(p)≤ofReal(q) exactly when p≤q or p≤0. The extra alternative accounts for clipping: a nonpositive lower input becomes zero, which lies below every output regardless of q. Thus the converted inequality can hold even when the original inequality fails, as for p=−1 and q=−2. Compared with [Faris §8.1 p88](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L151).

Converted real values satisfy ofReal(p)<ofReal(q) exactly when p<q and q>0. The upper input must be positive so that its output lies above zero. A negative lower input is allowed. Ordinary strict order alone is insufficient: −2<−1, but both converted values are zero, so their strict comparison fails. Compared with [Faris §8.1 p88](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L158).

With a nonnegative lower input p, the strict comparison of the converted values is equivalent to p<q. No independent positivity assumption on q is needed: p<q already makes q positive. If q is nonpositive, both comparisons are false. This preserves strict comparisons on the stated domain without claiming strict monotonicity across negative inputs. Compared with [Faris §8.1 p88](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L171).

Conversion into extended nonnegative reals preserves a product when the second real factor is nonnegative; the first may have either sign. If the first is negative, both sides become zero. Allowing both factors to be negative would fail: ofReal((−1)(−1)) is 1, while ofReal(−1)·ofReal(−1) is 0. Compared with [Faris §8.1 p88](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L301).

A real number converts to a nonzero extended nonnegative value exactly when it is strictly positive. Merely being nonzero is insufficient: negative real inputs are sent to zero. Every converted value is finite, so this criterion never includes infinity and agrees with the ordinary positive part max(r,0). Compared with [Faris §8.1 p88](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L189).

For any module M over a commutative ring R and linear functional φ:M→R, this is the complex with degree-n term ∧ⁿM and degree-lowering contraction by φ. Alternating deletion gives the signs; its first differential is φ. Finite sequences specialize via φ(v)=Σxᵢvᵢ. Neither freeness nor regularity is required for this definition. See [Stacks, Definition 15.29.1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0622) and [Definition 15.29.2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0623). Checks pass: singleton R —x→ R through [the first differential](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/KoszulComplex/Basic.lean#L120) and [higher-term vanishing](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/ExteriorPower/Basic.lean#L82); [the empty-sequence computation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/KoszulComplex/Regular.lean#L141) gives R in degree 0.
The first differential is exactly φ
The actual finite-free exterior terms vanish above rank
Contraction has the alternating-deletion signs
Consecutive differentials compose to zero
